label: prop:surreal-rate-calculus
title: Surreal rate calculus for the classical-limit scaling laws
html:
Proposition (conditional on conj:q-aubin-lions, conj:ns-counterexample, conj:critical-exponent, prop:blowup-yekutieli, and conj:regularity-breakdown; "Surreal rate calculus").

Let \varepsilon = 1/\omega > 0 be the Reeb infinitesimal, q = 1 + \varepsilon, and let \Delta_q \asymp \tfrac{1}{2}\varepsilon^3 (mass gap) and \Omega_q \asymp \varepsilon^{-1} (Reeb period) be the classical-limit scalings of collapse of the quantum gap. In \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon) the following strict inequalities hold:

  \Delta_q > 0, \qquad \Omega_q > 0, \qquad \Delta_q < \lambda < \Omega_q, \qquad \delta^2\,\Omega_q > \Delta_q
  \qquad (\forall\, \lambda, \delta \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}).
  1. Positivity: \Delta_q > 0 and \Omega_q > 0.
  2. Infinitesimal gap: \Delta_q < \lambda for every standard real \lambda > 0.
  3. Transfinite period: \Omega_q > \lambda for every standard real \lambda > 0.
  4. Squeeze (see surreal squeeze): for every standard real \delta > 0, \delta^2 \cdot \Omega_q > \Delta_q strictly in \mathbb{R}(\varepsilon).
